Oh, so No Man's Sky DOES have gameplay! Look at the retarded Pony finally being released from this mental torture. No more need to spin!

I don't know. Setting aside the snark for a second, that still sounds like it might be pretty boring in practice.

Obviously, the only way planets will be planet-sized (which I doubt) is if they're all being randomly generated, and if the algorithms aren't fine tuned, you could end up with empty, samey planets of different colors and identifiable, individual parts combined in uninteresting ways. And even if that works out, there needs to be more than just planet and space police to meaningfully interact with or the game will get old fast.

The comparisons to Minecraft and Terraria need to be justified with more info. Terraria has a specific way to progress in the main path, even if it's open-ended. That structure benefits the game. Does NMS have any structure besides "find the center of the galaxy?" Minecraft has a survival system that keeps you looking for resources. What does NMS have? The search for more space shekels?
It's a small indie game that I am sure could be enjoyable, good but because Sony has nothing else they hyped it too much, expect tons of buyers remorse and pissed off gamers.

I present to you my South Korean V-twin!
Looks sorta like an SV650. How does it ride?

Good eye! It is largely based off of a SV650. See, Hyosung corp. had been designing motors/frames/ parts for the major motorcycle manufacturers for many years when finally they said, since we've got all the tools, the machines, and people, why don't we just make our own bikes? I believe they started importing them to the United states in the mid 90's. Similar to Kia, or Hyundai, initial offerings were plagued with design flaws but Hyosung quickly got their act together and put together what I would consider a well built V-twin standard. The Pre fuel injected models are the ones I'm told to be weary of but I think they were phased out around 2008-2010

The only other bike I owned before the Hyo was a Suzuki Dr-Z 250 supermoto (what a riot that bike was!!) so its hard to compare the two. I would say the Hyo has a solid motor, excellent pickup and torquey all through the power band... The handling is alright for the street but a common upgrade is swapping out the rear shock for something better (suzuki bandit, gsxr, zx6), its water cooled, fuel injected and I think shes sexy as can be! The frame is a bit dated though and its steel in a time where I believe most companies have switched to alloys. I've upgraded the ECU (stock fueling was meh at best) with an Electronic Jet Kit, opened up the exhaust with a JRE Can, and added a K&N performance filter. The bike is pretty damn fast up to about 80-90 MPH, reckon with a good launch I could stick with a 600cc 4cyl till about 80 or so

Hey There, Congrats on the 650 :D I just got a 250r and love the bike so much. I am actually really impressed by hyosung and how far they have come. Just took my bike on the twisties for the first time and it rocked! Beautiful bike
